about.title: About Me
about.subtitle: From Accounting to Building SaaS Products

paragraphs.p1: I didn't take the traditional path into tech. My career started in accounting and finance, where I learned to think in systems — tracking flows, balancing inputs and outputs, and understanding how small errors compound into big problems.
paragraphs.p2: That analytical mindset followed me when I made the leap into software development. Self-taught and driven, I spent years mastering the fundamentals: JavaScript, TypeScript, design patterns, and architecture principles — before ever touching a framework.
paragraphs.p3: Today, I'm the CEO & Co-Founder of NevadaTech, where we help businesses transform their operations through technology. I architect systems using Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, and Domain-Driven Design — because I believe the structure of your code should reflect the structure of your business.
paragraphs.p4: When I'm not building products, I'm mentoring developers and advocating for a foundation-first approach to learning. The shortcuts don't work. The fundamentals always win.

howIThink.title: How I Think
howIThink.subtitle: My approach to building software
howIThink.intro: I don't start with code. I start with the problem. Every project begins with understanding the domain, defining boundaries, and choosing the right patterns — before a single line is written.

domain.title: Understand the Domain
domain.description: Before writing code, I immerse myself in the business problem. Who are the users? What are the pain points? What does success look like? The best architecture comes from deeply understanding what you're building.

boundaries.title: Define Boundaries
boundaries.description: I break complex systems into bounded contexts. Each module owns its domain, exposes clear interfaces, and hides its implementation. This is where Hexagonal Architecture and DDD shine.

patterns.title: Choose Patterns Intentionally
patterns.description: Not every project needs DDD. Not every API needs GraphQL. I choose patterns based on the problem's complexity, the team's expertise, and the project's lifecycle. The right tool, not the trendy one.

build.title: Build with Confidence
build.description: Tests aren't an afterthought — they're part of the design. 97% coverage on my inventory system isn't vanity; it's the confidence to refactor, scale, and ship without fear.

iterate.title: Ship and Iterate
iterate.description: Perfect is the enemy of shipped. I build MVPs, gather feedback, and iterate. But I never sacrifice architecture for speed — because technical debt always comes due.

inventory.title: Nevada Inventory System
inventory.subtitle: How I Designed a Multi-Tenant SaaS from Scratch

problem.title: The Problem
problem.content: Businesses managing inventory across multiple warehouses relied on spreadsheets and disconnected tools. They needed real-time visibility, traceability, and role-based access — all in one platform that could scale.

approach.title: The Approach
approach.content: I started by mapping the domain: warehouses, products, stock movements, organizations. Each concept became a bounded context. The architecture had to support multi-tenancy from day one — not bolted on later.

items.title: Why Hexagonal Architecture?
items.content: The business logic needed to be completely isolated from infrastructure concerns. By using ports and adapters, the domain layer doesn't know about HTTP, databases, or external APIs. This made testing straightforward and refactoring safe.

items.title: Why DDD + Screaming Architecture?
items.content: The folder structure screams 'inventory management', not 'NestJS app'. Modules are organized by domain concept (products, warehouses, movements), not by technical layer. Any developer opening the codebase immediately understands what it does.

items.title: Multi-Tenant Data Isolation
items.content: Every query filters by organization. Every endpoint validates tenant ownership. The RBAC system with 80+ granular permissions ensures users only access what they should — down to individual warehouse operations.

items.title: VTEX Integration
items.content: The system syncs with VTEX for e-commerce order management. Products, orders, and fulfillment flow bidirectionally. This required careful idempotency design to handle retries and webhook failures.

build.title: The Build
build.content: The backend uses NestJS 11 with Prisma 7 and PostgreSQL. Redis handles caching and rate limiting. The frontend is built with Next.js 16, React 19, and Tailwind CSS 4, following the same hexagonal principles with a BFF (Backend for Frontend) pattern. The system generates 17 types of reports in PDF, Excel, and CSV formats.

result.title: The Result
result.content: A production SaaS platform with a real paying client, designed to handle 50+ warehouses and 100,000+ products. The backend has 7,749 tests with 97% coverage — not as vanity, but as the confidence to ship features without fear.

scheduler.title: Meeting Scheduler
scheduler.subtitle: How I Built a Fair Assignment Engine with Zero Side Effects

problem.title: The Problem
problem.content: Congregation meetings require weekly assignment scheduling — assigning speakers, readers, and attendants across multiple meeting types. This was done manually with spreadsheets, leading to unfair distributions, conflicts, and hours of administrative work every week.

approach.title: The Approach
approach.content: The core challenge wasn't the UI — it was the assignment algorithm. I needed a system that could produce fair, conflict-free assignments automatically, while respecting eligibility rules, gender constraints, and role-based requirements. And it had to be deterministic and testable.

items.title: Why a Pure Assignment Engine?
items.content: The assignment engine is a pure function: it takes input (publishers, meetings, constraints) and returns output (assignments) with zero side effects. No database access, no API calls. This makes it infinitely testable and completely predictable.

items.title: Why LRU Rotation?
items.content: Fairness isn't random — it's systematic. The LRU (Least Recently Used) algorithm ensures that whoever hasn't been assigned recently gets priority. Combined with priority ordering (most restrictive parts first), the algorithm guarantees fair distribution across all participants.

items.title: Two-Pass Assignment System
items.content: The engine runs two passes: main assignees first, then helpers. This prevents conflicts where a helper assignment might block a more critical main assignment. The priority ordering ensures the most constrained parts get filled first.

build.title: The Build
build.content: Built with Next.js 16.2, TypeScript 5, and Tailwind CSS 4. The application handles midweek meetings, weekend meetings, and attendant/microphone rotation — all with automatic assignment and full manual override capability. It generates printable S-140 and S-89 forms and supports CSV import/export for easy migration.

result.title: The Result
result.content: What used to take hours of manual spreadsheet work now happens in seconds. The algorithm produces conflict-free, fair assignments every time. Publishers see their assignments clearly, history is tracked, and workload distribution is transparent.

nevadatech.title: NevadaTech
nevadatech.subtitle: From Accountant to CEO: Founding a Tech Company

problem.title: The Opportunity
problem.content: Businesses in Latin America — especially startups and SMEs — struggle to find reliable technology partners who understand both the technical and business sides. Many agencies deliver code without understanding the problem they're solving.

approach.title: The Vision
approach.content: We founded NevadaTech with a clear philosophy: technology should be a strategic ally, not just a deliverable. Every project starts with understanding the business problem, then designing the right solution — not the other way around.

items.title: Complementary Co-Founders
items.content: I brought full-stack development and product vision as CEO. Andres Santana joined as CTO with deep frontend and UX expertise. Marlon Ramirez as COO handles backend and operations. Together, we cover the full spectrum — design, development, and delivery.

items.title: Service-First, Then Products
items.content: We started with client services to build cash flow and reputation, while developing our own products (like the Inventory System) in parallel. This dual approach reduces risk and creates recurring revenue opportunities.

items.title: Remote-First Culture
items.content: From day one, we built a remote-first culture with async communication, clear ownership, and honest feedback. This lets us hire the best talent regardless of location and serve clients across different time zones.

build.title: What We've Built
build.content: NevadaTech serves clients across fintech, healthcare, e-commerce, and education. We deliver web applications, mobile apps, cloud infrastructure, and AI-driven solutions. Our tech stack centers on React, Next.js, Node.js, Python, and AWS/GCP.

result.title: Where We Are Today
result.content: We've delivered projects for clients like Bambu Coliving, ToPra, FZ Academia, and VR Experience. Our own SaaS products are gaining traction. And we're just getting started — the LatAm tech ecosystem is full of opportunity for teams that prioritize quality over speed.
